In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the human rights of individuals are to be protected in a differentiated society.2

the following questions: (1) What is the relationship between human rights, law and justice? (2) What is the nature of the modern society that threatens human rights? (3) What is the role of law in protecting human rights in modern society?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the law of human rights is a legal form of the struggle for justice in a society which, through its own self-reproductive dynamics, threatens to become a society of the dead.
modern society, in its differentiated form, is not a society of human beings, but rather a society of communications.

human rights are an expression of a legal system's self-assertion against the threat of destruction of its own integrity by the autonomous communication systems of modern society, and that human rights are a legal system's way of realising the law-transcending justice claims of human beings endangered by modern communication systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the human rights of the individual are a way of ensuring the self-reproduction of modern society, by protecting its members from the destructive effects of its communications.2

The main takeaway from our work is that

the current state of the art in human rights is not a good fit for human rights.2 The main takeaway from this paper is that the current status quo of the human rights is not the same as the current state of affairs in the human rights literature.
the human rights discourse is not only a discourse about rights, but it is also a discourse that has the potential to shape the way people think about themselves and the way they relate to others.
